newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-FONSECA AND BALBO LIFT ROMA INTO EARLY SERIE A LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FONSECA AND BALBO LIFT ROMA INTO EARLY SERIE A LEAD.

text.p: Goals from Uruguay's Daniel Fonseca and Argentine Abel Balbo lifted Roma to the top of Italy's Serie A on Sunday as the Rome side kept up their perfect start to the season with a 2-0 win at Vicenza.
With a maximum six points from two matches, Roma are level on points with Bologna and Inter, winners over Verona and Perugia respectively, but lead the table on goal difference.
Bologna, second division champions last season, continued their impressive return to the top flight with a convincing 2-0 win at Verona with goals from Russian Igor Kolyvanov and Carlo Nervo.

Roy Hodgson's expensively assembled Inter side struggled to a 1-0 win over Perugia at the San Siro, relying on some fine goalkeeping from Gianluca Pagliuca and a solo effort from Argentine midfielder Javier Zanetti to grab all three points.
Champions Milan, beaten 3-2 at home by Porto in the European Cup last week, can join Roma, Bologna and Inter at the top if they win at Sampdoria later on Sunday.
European Cup holders Juventus lie joint fourth with Parma - held 0-0 at Piacenza - after defeating Cagliari in Turin, 2-1.
Croat Alen Boksic, on target against Manchester United last week, opened the scoring in the ninth minute with Italy defender Ciro Ferrara adding a second in the 58th.
Lazio, who entertained championship ambitions at the start of the season, lie bottom after stumbling to their second successive defeat.
The Roman side, beaten at Bologna last week, slipped to a shock 1-0 home defeat at the hands of Udinese for whom Giovanni Bia scored a second-half penalty.
Fonseca's second goal of the season owed much to Italy under-21 international Damiano Tommasi, who scored twice in Roma's 3-0 victory over Dynamo Moscow in the UEFA Cup last week.
Tommasi released Fonseca in the 32nd minute with a header lobbed over the Vicenza defence, and the Uruguayan volleyed home with lethal precision.
Balbo sealed Roma's win after latching on to Swede Martin Dahlin's defence-splitting pass.
The San Siro was treated to another superb piece of individual skill to add to George Weah's end-to-end solo goal for Milan last weekend.
Inter's Zanetti started a run close to the halfway line, exchanged passes with Paul Ince and then dribbled past three Perugia defenders before beating goalkeeper Alexander Kocic.
Before and after Zanetti's goal, former international goalkeeper Pagliuca kept Inter in the lead with a series of fine reflex saves, the last in the dying minutes from Massimiliano Allegri.
Juve's Boksic was criticised for poor finishing after his side's disappointing draw at Reggiana last week but in the past seven days the Croat has silenced his critics with two goals.
Against Cagliari he ran on to a delightful through-ball from Alessandro Del Piero, drew Swiss goalkeeper Marco Pascolo and drilled a low diagonal shot into the opposite corner.
At the Olympic stadium, Zdenek Zeman's rebuilt Lazio side continued its dire start to the season.

Pierluigi Casiraghi saw a close-range volley hit the post in the 62nd minute and then Dario Marcolin brought down German international Oliver Bierhoff, allowing Bia to score from the penalty spot for Udinese's victory.
At Bergamo, in a repeat of last season's Italian Cup final, only a late headed goal from Argentine Gabriel Batistuta spared Fiorentina from their second successive defeat, this time against Atalanta.
Luis Oliveira gave the visitors a 16th-minute lead before Felippo Inzaghi, with two goals in four minutes, threatened to steal all three points for Atalanta.
